# Flightroom

> Build, ship and run your whole product on Kubernetes.

Flightroom (formerly MFE Orchestrator) is an open-source platform that takes micro
frontends and backend services from template to Kubernetes. It versions every
build, releases micro frontends without rebuilding the host, deploys services
through GitOps with Argo CD, and lets anyone on the team describe a change in
plain language and get it back as a pull request. It runs as a hosted console or
self-hosted with Docker, Docker Compose, a Helm chart on Kubernetes, or
Terraform/OpenTofu. License: Apache-2.0.

Category: open-source platform for micro frontends and services on Kubernetes.
Also written: micro-frontend, microfrontend. MFE stands for micro frontend.

This file is a pointer. The documentation is served from mfe-orchestrator.dev/documentation for now and
carries its own llms.txt, which indexes every page.

## Documentation

- [llms.txt](https://mfe-orchestrator.dev/documentation/llms.txt): index of every documentation page, each with a one-line description
- [llms-full.txt](https://mfe-orchestrator.dev/documentation/llms-full.txt): the full markdown of every documentation page, in one file
- [Documentation home](https://mfe-orchestrator.dev/documentation/): the HTML documentation

## Product

- [Flightroom](https://flightroom.dev/): product site
- [Console](https://console.flightroom.dev/): the hosted console
- [GitHub](https://github.com/flightroom): source, templates and CI integrations

## Pillars

- [Micro frontends](https://flightroom.dev/micro-frontends): independent releases without rebuilding the host, immutable snapshots, rollback, canary releases, per-environment variables, Module Federation config for Vite and Webpack
- [Kubernetes](https://flightroom.dev/kubernetes): GitOps deploys with Argo CD, backend services from templates, environments as namespaces, Gateway API exposure
- [AI](https://flightroom.dev/ai): describe a change in plain language and get a pull request, bring your own model, remote MCP server

## Concepts

- [What is a micro frontend (MFE)?](https://flightroom.dev/what-is-a-micro-frontend): definition of the term, the architecture, its trade-offs and when it is worth adopting
- [Module Federation versioning and dynamic remotes](https://flightroom.dev/module-federation): why Module Federation alone leaves version selection to you, and how Flightroom replaces a hand-maintained remotes file
- [FAQ](https://flightroom.dev/faq): common questions on micro frontends, Kubernetes deploys, AI changes and self-hosting
- [Get started](https://flightroom.dev/start-now): the hosted console, or self-hosting
- [About](https://flightroom.dev/about): why the project exists and how it grew from MFE Orchestrator
